notes.text: button, input text-like controls including size attributes, input button/reset/submit, checkbox, radio, range, color, hidden, file, image with explicit attributes, select including size/multiple attributes, progress, and meter intrinsic sizes have parity coverage as independently positioned controls. Time inputs and textareas have exact parity coverage when author-sized.
Common form controls are measured as replaced leaves so option children and anonymous control internals do not participate in the layout tree.

Intrinsic native-control geometry comes from an explicitly selected deterministic profile. The portable profile preserves the package's existing cross-host defaults; profiles never follow the runtime host automatically. Per-control metric overrides merge onto the selected profile and can replace every metric to define custom geometry.

The full native-control fixture is checked exactly against the selected portable engine profile on every host and against committed Chromium 147 snapshots on the recorded Linux, macOS, and Windows CI runner families. Local Chromium is observed but not matched to a CI snapshot because fonts and themes can change native metrics within the same operating system.
The intrinsic width of input[type=time] depends on Chromium's host-native picker UI, so its deterministic default is not claimed as cross-platform pixel parity.
Native textarea dimensions derived from default rows/cols depend on Chromium host font metrics, so deterministic intrinsic textarea dimensions are not claimed as cross-platform pixel parity.
Inline form-control formatting, fieldset and legend layout, option popup layout, placeholder text, and most control-specific UA styling are not modeled.
